similar_scenes.name: Indie, C86 y el giro retro
similar_scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
similar_scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
similar_scenes.desc: En 1985 la energía se ha disipado: el new pop cae en la decadencia (Live Aid, «una tragedia para el pop»), los singles independientes venden la mitad que en 1980 y «independiente» se convierte en «indie», un género de guitarras sucias, voces pálidas y nostalgia de los sesenta, oposición impotente al mainstream. El futurismo da paso al «rock de coleccionista»: The Jesus and Mary Chain (Psychocandy: Ronettes y Beach Boys con feedback), el sello Creation y Primal Scream, la cassette C86 de NME (The Pastels, Shop Assistants, The Soup Dragons, June Brides) y su culto a la inocencia, que reaparecerá en el riot grrrl. The Smiths y R.E.M., contra los ochenta; Hüsker Dü, Sonic Youth, Butthole Surfers y Dinosaur Jr. redescubren el acid rock; de ahí, Nirvana.

similar_scenes.name: Post-rock: Tortoise y la electrónica del indie
similar_scenes.book: Techno Rebels: The Renegades of Electronic Funk
similar_scenes.author: Dan Sicko
similar_scenes.desc: Otra salida para la evolución del techno, mal nombrada: una extensión de las estructuras del rock con apariencia de banda. Míchigan es uno de sus centros (His Name Is Alive, de Livonia, en 4AD; Windy & Carl), aunque apenas ha conectado con el techno de Detroit. Tortoise, formado en Chicago en 1990 por miembros de una docena de bandas y anclado en el batería John McEntire, renunció a guitarras y voces: en directo, vibráfonos, marimbas, guitarras de pedal, sintetizadores y cajas de ritmos para una mezcla de música de baile desenrollada, dub y bandas sonoras, con temas que migran de un proyecto a otro («Jetty», de «La Jetee» de Isotope 217). El indie acabó abrazando la electrónica: Postal Service, Four Tet, Caribou, Broadcast.

podcast.title: "Selling Out" Perception
podcast.body: Within certain segments of the indie world, profiting from music is often viewed as "wrong" and a betrayal of artistic ideals and principles. This perspective suggests that money compromises the purity of the relationship between the artist and their music, as well as with their fans.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Concept of Selling Out: Part 2

podcast.title: Band T-Shirt Concert Etiquette
podcast.body: In the Indy Rock genre, it is generally considered "uncool" to wear a band's t-shirt to their own concert, possibly because it might suggest being "too much of a fan" or not "cool enough." "However, if you want to look at Indy Rock, it seems that it is generally considered uncool to wear shirt to show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Survey Says: Useful and Odd Music Surveys and Polls

podcast.title: Basic Enduring Sound
podcast.body: Indie music is listed as one of the basic and enduring sounds that will never go away, but is continuously challenged by new genres. "The basic sounds are still with us. Rock, alternative, indie, Goth, industrial, metal, synth-based music, ska, reggae, and so on. They're never going to go away."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

podcast.title: British Equivalent of Alternative
podcast.body: Originally, "indie" in the UK was the equivalent of the North American term "alternative," referring to music from small record labels not owned by major multinational companies. The UK maintained this usage even as North America embraced "alternative nation" in the 1990s. "See originally indie was the British equivalent of the North American term alternative."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rock Snob

podcast.title: British Indie Identity
podcast.body: The Chemical Brothers' body of work, notably exemplified by their collaboration with Richard Ashcroft on "The Test," is seen as perfectly embodying the British indie sound, characterized by its seamless blend of electronic and rock elements. "está en el camino exacto entre la electrónica y la música rock, la sígabritamica."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Las mejores colaboraciones y remezclas de The Chemical Brothers

podcast.title: Calm Style
podcast.body: Efrim Manuel Menuck's album *Trans-Alegic Exogus* is described as typical, calm indie music. "típica banda, un Indy, la verdad es que está bastante bien así, poca indita, al tranquilillo."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Lanzamientos Febrero  2018

podcast.title: Challenges in Early 1990s
podcast.body: In the early 1990s, operating as an indie group was considered a significant risk due to the prevailing belief among rock fans that successful bands would naturally secure major label deals. This attitude created a challenging environment for independent artists. "The fact that you were still in the indie just meant that you weren't worth anyone's time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the '90s: Part 1

podcast.title: Combative Rejection of Rave
podcast.body: The indie scene shared the rock scene's combative stance against rave culture, initially creating resistance for electronic acts attempting to bridge the gap. "la gente que estaba dentro de los bares y discotecas roc tenía un movimiento muy combativo y muy rechazado hace toda la cultura rey."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: The Chemical Brothers. Padres de la cultura BIG BEAT

podcast.title: Composer Style for Johnny Greenwood
podcast.body: Johnny Greenwood works in indie styles as a composer for movie, TV, and documentary soundtracks. "This guy can work in a variety of styles. Rock, indie, jazz, chamber orchestra, and full-on classical music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Modern Guitar Heroes:  The Men

podcast.title: DIY Ethic
podcast.body: A crucial aspect of being indie is the "do it yourself" (DIY) ethic. Without the extensive infrastructure of a massive label, artists and those committed to distributing their music often have to handle much of the business and marketing themselves, acting as independent business people. "Another aspect of being Indy is the do it yourself, Ethic."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 1

podcast.title: Definition of Independent (Indie)
podcast.body: "Indie" is short for independent, referring to music from artists not directly signed to one of the major multinational record labels (Universal, Sony, Warner). Artists recording for any other label, or operating independently of the three majors, are considered indie. The term describes a type of record company, its signed artists, and the music they create, having nothing to do with a band's sound or record sales. "Indy is, of course, short for independent. This means we're dealing with music from artists who are not signed directly to one of the major multinational record labels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 1

podcast.title: Distribution Deals with Majors
podcast.body: Many indie acts that gained prominence in the 2010s came from indie labels that maintained distribution deals with major labels. "In many cases, these acts came from the world of indie labels who had distribution deals with the major labels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Dreampop Integration
podcast.body: Dreampop deeply integrated into the indie and independent music scenes, contributing to its lasting legacy and reach. "se adentro mucho en lo que se gara rama más indie, más independiente."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: DREAM POP y SHOEGAZE. Diferencias entre ellos.

podcast.title: Early Tiny Desk Focus
podcast.body: In its early days, Tiny Desk almost exclusively focused on the indie scene, featuring bands like Arcade Fire and Wilco. This initial specialization helped establish its reputation before it expanded to other genres. "En sus inicios, Ténidé es que se centraba casi exclusivamente en la escena Indy, por ahí pasaban bandas como el ancho o builco."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: De Tiny Desk a Boiler Room: El Boom de los Conciertos en YouTube

podcast.title: Evolution into Mainstream Influence
podcast.body: By the early 1990s, indie and alternative music began to be taken very seriously. As the number of major labels decreased, the power and importance of independent labels gained more attention, shifting the dynamic of the music industry. "For the early 90s, people had begun to take Indie and alternative music very, very seriously. And as the number of major label shrunk, more attention was paid to the power and importance of independent labels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

podcast.title: Evolution of Labels (Historical Context)
podcast.body: Initially, all record labels were considered indie, with thousands existing in America alone in the early 1960s (at least 3,000). Over time, larger labels acquired smaller ones, merged, or went out of business, consolidating the industry. By the 1970s, there were six or seven major labels, which has since reduced to just three (Universal, Sony, Warner) today. "Now once upon a time, all record labels were Indy. They were some that were bigger than others like Deca and London and RCA and EMI, but there were literally thousands of small labels that did their own thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 1

podcast.title: Growth of Independent Labels
podcast.body: The independent label scene became crucial for bands like Bauhaus in post-punk England, with "small nimble indie labels" appearing almost daily, capable of quickly signing and promoting new sounds and trends. "Bauhaus and Bella Logosi's dead, at least on beggars banquet, another one of those small nimble indie labels that popped up almost daily in post-punk England."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 7

podcast.title: Historical Perception and Growth
podcast.body: Not long ago, indie music was widely ignored, with the belief that any good music would be picked up by a major label. It was often seen as the domain of "weirdos and outliers," not good enough for broad enjoyment. However, this allowed it to grow in its "Petri dish" without capitalistic interference, to the point where it could no longer be ignored by the early 1990s. "There was a time, not that long ago, when indie music was ignored by most people. The thinking was that if the music was any good, then it would have been picked up and released by a major label, right?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

podcast.title: Importance in the 2010s
podcast.body: Indie music, and material from artists not directly signed to major labels, constituted an important aspect of the music of the 2010s. Without the sheer volume of new music and crafty distribution by indie-friendly companies, the decade would have been "pretty empty." "Indie music, or at least material from artists not directly signed to one of the three majors, was an important aspect to the music of the 2010s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Influence on Mainstream Rock
podcast.body: The styles and trends introduced by independent musicians significantly influenced major label mainstream rock, which would have been "much different" without their contributions. "And without the influence of independent musicians and the styles and trends that they brought along with them, major label mainstream rock would have been much different."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Injecting New Life into Rock (Early 2000s)
podcast.body: In the early 2000s, indie music played a crucial role in revitalizing a rock scene that had become "more-bun." It helped inject new energy and sounds into the genre. "So far, we've looked at how indie music injected new life into a more-bun rock scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00s Part 4: Variety Returns

podcast.title: Later Terminology
podcast.body: The word "indie" emerged as a term slightly later than "post punk" to describe the music evolving from the original punk scene. "The word that came a little later was indie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 7

podcast.title: Major Label Subsidiaries
podcast.body: Many subsidiary labels of the major corporations often adopt the appearance and feel of indie labels, frequently by design, but they are still considered part of the major label machine. This allows for a perceived independent image while still being part of a larger corporate structure. "Many of those subsidiaries have the look and feel of an Indy label, and often that's very much by design, but they are still considered to be part of the major label machine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 1

podcast.title: Major Part of 2010s Soundtrack
podcast.body: Indie music played a major role in the soundtrack of the 2010s, characterized by interesting trends and commonalities. "Indie music was a major part of our soundtrack for the 2010s, and there were some interesting trends and commonalities."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Manchester Scene Fusion
podcast.body: Indie music, alongside rock, played a role in the Manchester music scene where early House and Techno influences began to mix, as evidenced by bands like New Order and The Stone Roses. "esa relación en la que es electrónica House de mezcla con la música rock, la música indibrita."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: The Chemical Brothers. Padres de la cultura BIG BEAT

podcast.title: Market Dominance in Streaming Era
podcast.body: Despite traditional wisdom, independent labels and do-it-yourself musicians account for approximately 96% of all new music uploaded to streaming services daily, a significant shift from the 4% contributed by major labels. "96% of all new music comes from independent musicians."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Modern North American Meaning
podcast.body: Today in North America, "indie" essentially refers to music from artists working within an expanding network of labels not associated with the four major labels. However, it has also evolved to describe a certain aesthetic, sensibility, and even a sound, regardless of label origin, sometimes even originating from a major label, especially given distribution deals between independents and majors. "Well essentially it means any music from artists who work within an expanding network of record labels that aren't associated with the four remaining major labels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rock Snob

podcast.title: MySpace Artist Style
podcast.body: Indie was identified as one of the distinctive styles associated with "MySpace Artists." The platform's direct artist-to-fan interaction fostered communities around genres like indie, contributing to their popularization and the launch of new acts. "Before long, we had something called MySpace Artists, a distinctive set of styles that involved pop punk, emo, and indie acts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 1: (100-91)

podcast.title: Rising Market Share
podcast.body: The market share for indie labels has been increasing by double digits for nearly 25 years. "The market share for indie labels has been rising by double digits for almost 25 years now."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Spanish Indie Bands
podcast.body: Several notable Spanish bands are categorized under indie, including Dorian, identified as one of the best indie bands in Spain. "una de las mejores bandas indis que hemos tenido en España."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Record Store Day 2018. Resumen de lanzamientos.

podcast.title: Spotify Resistance
podcast.body: Indie groups like The Black Keys and Placebo have been notable for their initial resistance to Spotify, only to eventually yield and make their discographies available on the platform, often due to shared rights issues. "grupos medios, medio indíscomo pueden ser los Blackis o placebo que también han sido grandes enemigos. Spotify"

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Artistas que no están en Spotify y por qué

podcast.title: Studying Aid for High Achievers
podcast.body: Indie music was identified as the third genre listened to by students who achieved the highest grades, suggesting it is effective for studying. "and number three, indie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Survey Says: Useful and Odd Music Surveys and Polls

podcast.title: UK Dominance in Early 1990s
podcast.body: At the beginning of the 1990s, The Stone Roses were recognized as the biggest Indie band in the UK, signaling the genre's significant popularity and influence during that specific period. "At the beginning of the 1990s the biggest Indie band in the UK was the Stone Roses."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Legendary Gigs

podcast.title: UK Record Charts Influence
podcast.body: The UK music scene favored the term "indie" partly due to their love for record charts, with an official independent record chart existing since at least 1980, publicizing the progress of indie artists weekly. "An official independent record chart had been part of the music culture since at least 1980."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rock Snob

podcast.title: Underground Cred and Self-Promotion
podcast.body: Some artists aim to maintain "original underground cred" by avoiding traditional label structures, instead using platforms like blogs, Myspace, Facebook, YouTube, SoundCloud, and Bandcamp for promotion and distribution. "They want to keep their original underground cred and find alternate ways of promoting themselves and distributing their music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rock Snob
